refs.note: James’s “The Will to Believe” taught — genuine options and the right to believe

John Kaag reads James's 1895 talk 'Is Life Worth Living?' as advice for someone in despair: James's answer is 'maybe', and Kaag argues that the maybe is where meaning lives, since the things that keep a life going all carry risk. It shows the will to believe at work on the hardest question a person can face. The talk speaks openly about suicide; the lecture is followed by audience questions.

refs.note: Dewey on the quest for certainty and its costs, taught

Two Dewey scholars read Dewey as a philosopher of a way of life. Experience, for Dewey, is the process of growth: you act, something happens, and when the result is not what you wanted, doubt comes up and your habits have to be rebuilt. The talk then asks what the shared, social version of a personal practice would look like. Watch the talk; the open discussion that follows is optional.
